Suppose $\dsn{X} \siid \ndist{\mean, \varpar}$ with $\varpar$ known,
and we want to predict the mean $\bar X^*$ of $m$ new observations
from the same distribution,
independent of the first $n$.
The MLE of $\mean$ is $\hmean = \bar X$,
and the difference $\bar X^* - \hmean$
(the negative of the [prediction error](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-error))
is a difference of independent Gaussian variables, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Var{\bar X^* - \hmean}
&= \Var{\bar X^*} + \Var{\hmean}
&& \text{(variance of a difference of independent variables)}\\
&= \frac{\varpar}{m} + \frac{\varpar}{n}
&& \text{(variance of a sample mean)}
\end{aligned}
$$

and $\bar X^* - \hmean \sim \ndist{0, \varpar\paren{\frac{1}{m} + \frac{1}{n}}}$.
So a $100(1 - \siglevel)\%$ prediction interval for $\bar X^*$ is:

$$\hmean \pm z_{1 - \siglevel/2} \, \sdpar \sqrt{\frac{1}{m} + \frac{1}{n}}$$

Usually $m = 1$.
The term $1/n$ accounts for the uncertainty in $\hmean$,
and becomes negligible when $n$ is much larger than $m$.
